title: Technical MCQ Set 06: Design Patterns, B-Trees & Scheduling
description: Covers Java enums/ThreadLocal/LRU LinkedHashMap, SQL duplicate detection, B-Tree height numerical, SJF scheduling, CIDR supernetting, and MST.

questions.question: What keys remain in `cache` (in iteration order) after running this Java code?
questions.explanation: Passing `accessOrder = true` makes `LinkedHashMap` maintain LRU order: `put(1), put(2)` -> `[1, 2]`; `get(1)` moves `1` to most-recent -> `[2, 1]`; `put(3)` triggers `removeEldestEntry` which evicts `2`, leaving `[1, 3]`.

questions.question: What happens when compiling the following Java constructor?
options: Compilation error: call to `super` must be first statement in constructor
questions.explanation: In Java (prior to flexible constructor bodies preview), `super(...)` or `this(...)` must be the very first statement in a constructor; placing `System.out.println` before `super(10)` triggers a compile-time error.

questions.subtopic: ThreadLocal Memory Leak in Thread Pools
questions.question: Why can failing to call `threadLocal.remove()` in a Spring Boot / Tomcat web filter cause memory leaks in production?
options: `ThreadLocal` converts heap objects into off-heap native memory
Servlet container worker threads are pooled and live indefinitely, keeping strong references to `ThreadLocalMap` values across requests
`ThreadLocal` disables garbage collection across the entire JVM
questions.explanation: In a `ThreadLocalMap`, the key is a weak reference to the `ThreadLocal`, while the value is a STRONG reference. Pooled Tomcat threads never die, so unremoved values stay pinned in memory (and risk leaking tenant context to the next HTTP request).

questions.question: Why does Joshua Bloch's *Effective Java* recommend a single-element `enum` as the cleanest way to implement a Singleton in Java?
options: Enums can be instantiated dynamically using `new EnumSingleton()`
The JVM guarantees single-instance thread-safe initialization AND immunity to reflection and deserialization attacks out of the box
Enums automatically persist their state to JDBC databases
Enums support multiple inheritance of concrete classes
questions.explanation: Java prevents `Constructor.newInstance()` on enum types and handles enum deserialization by name lookup, preventing duplicate instances from reflection or `ObjectInputStream`.

questions.question: When is `CopyOnWriteArrayList` an ideal choice over `Collections.synchronizedList(new ArrayList<>())`?
options: Write-heavy workloads with thousands of `add`/`remove` calls per second
Read-heavy workloads with rare writes where lock-free, snapshot-consistent iteration without `ConcurrentModificationException` is needed
Implementing a FIFO queue with O(1) `poll()`
questions.explanation: `CopyOnWriteArrayList` duplicates the entire backing array on every mutation (`O(N)` write cost), making writes expensive but reads/iterators completely lock-free and immune to `ConcurrentModificationException`.

questions.question: Which SQL query returns every `email` appearing more than once in `Users(id, email)` along with its occurrence count?
options: `SELECT email, COUNT(*) FROM Users WHERE COUNT(*) > 1 GROUP BY email`
`SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Users GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`
`SELECT DISTINCT email, COUNT(*) FROM Users GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`
`SELECT email FROM Users GROUP BY email ORDER BY COUNT(*) > 1`
questions.explanation: Group by `email` and filter groups whose `COUNT(*) > 1` using `HAVING` (never `WHERE`, because aggregates cannot be evaluated row-by-row before grouping).

questions.question: Table `Sizes` has 4 rows and Table `Colors` has 5 rows. How many rows does `SELECT * FROM Sizes CROSS JOIN Colors;` produce?
questions.explanation: `CROSS JOIN` computes the Cartesian product of both tables: 4 * 5 = 20 rows.

questions.question: Schedule S has operations: `R1(X), R2(X), W1(X), W2(X)`. Is S conflict-serializable?
options: Yes, equivalent to serial order T1 -> T2
Yes, equivalent to serial order T2 -> T1
No, because the precedence graph contains a cycle `T1 <-> T2`
Yes, because neither transaction reads uncommitted data
questions.explanation: Conflicting pairs on `X`: `R2(X)` before `W1(X)` adds edge `T2 -> T1`; `R1(X)` before `W2(X)` adds edge `T1 -> T2`. The cycle `T1 -> T2 -> T1` proves S is NOT conflict-serializable.

questions.question: In a B-Tree of order `m = 5` (maximum 5 children per node), what are the MINIMUM and MAXIMUM number of keys allowed in any non-root internal node?
questions.explanation: A B-Tree of order `m` has at most `m` children (`m - 1 = 4` keys) and at least `ceil(m/2)` children (`ceil(5/2) - 1 = 3 - 1 = 2` keys) in non-root internal nodes.

questions.question: Four jobs arrive with (Arrival, Burst): J1(0, 6), J2(1, 3), J3(2, 8), J4(3, 2). Under non-preemptive Shortest Job First (SJF), what is the average turnaround time?
Which statement accurately compares fragmentation in pure Paging versus pure Segmentation?
options: Paging suffers from external fragmentation; Segmentation suffers from internal fragmentation
Paging eliminates external fragmentation (leaving minor internal fragmentation in the last page), whereas Segmentation suffers from external fragmentation
Both eliminate all internal and external fragmentation
Both require contiguous physical memory for the entire process
questions.explanation: Fixed-size page frames fit any free frame (no external fragmentation, only partial waste inside the last page). Variable-size segments leave scattered unallocated memory holes between segments (external fragmentation).

questions.question: A router needs to aggregate four contiguous `/24` networks: `198.51.100.0/24`, `198.51.101.0/24`, `198.51.102.0/24`, and `198.51.103.0/24` into a single summary CIDR route. Which summary prefix is exact?
questions.explanation: In binary, third octets 100..103 are `01100100`, `01100101`, `01100110`, `01100111`. They share the top 6 bits of the 3rd octet (`100` is divisible by 4). Total shared prefix = 8 + 8 + 6 = `/22` => `198.51.100.0/22`.

questions.question: What is the correct 4-step message sequence (DORA) when a client acquires an IPv4 lease from a DHCP server?
questions.explanation: DHCP follows DORA: Client broadcasts DHCPDISCOVER -> Server(s) reply DHCPOFFER -> Client selects and broadcasts DHCPREQUEST -> Chosen server confirms with DHCPACK.

questions.question: For finding a Minimum Spanning Tree on a VERY DENSE graph where `E ≈ V^2`, which algorithm + data structure combination achieves the better asymptotic time complexity?
options: Kruskal's with sorted edge list: `O(V^2 log V)`
Prim's using an adjacency matrix without a binary heap: `O(V^2)`
questions.explanation: For dense graphs (`E = Theta(V^2)`), adjacency-matrix Prim's takes `O(V^2)` without any `log V` factor, beating Kruskal's `O(E log E) = O(V^2 log V)`.

questions.question: What is the expected (average) time complexity of finding the Kth smallest element in an unsorted array of size `N` using randomized QuickSelect?
questions.explanation: Unlike QuickSort, QuickSelect recurses into only ONE partition each step. Expected work `N + N/2 + N/4 + ... = 2N = O(N)`.

questions.question: Which JDBC method retrieves column count, column names, and SQL column types dynamically from an arbitrary `ResultSet`?
questions.explanation: `resultSet.getMetaData()` returns a `ResultSetMetaData` object exposing `getColumnCount()`, `getColumnName(i)`, and `getColumnTypeName(i)` (1-indexed).

questions.question: In SOLID design, what does the Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) require?
options: Databases must call REST controllers directly
High-level business modules and low-level infrastructure modules should both depend on abstractions (interfaces), not concrete implementations
Every class must invert its inheritance hierarchy before deployment
Global static variables should replace dependency injection
questions.explanation: DIP decouples high-level policy (e.g., `OrderService`) from low-level details (e.g., `MySqlOrderRepo`) by having both depend on an abstraction (`OrderRepository` interface).

questions.question: Which three core annotations are bundled together by `@SpringBootApplication`?
questions.explanation: `@SpringBootApplication` combines `@SpringBootConfiguration` (a `@Configuration` variant), `@EnableAutoConfiguration`, and `@ComponentScan`.

questions.subtopic: Abstract Class vs Interface in Java 8+
questions.question: Even after Java 8 introduced `default` and `static` methods in interfaces, what capability remains exclusive to an `abstract class`?
options: Maintaining mutable non-static instance fields (`state`) and defining constructors to initialize them
Being implemented alongside multiple other types
questions.explanation: All fields in an interface are implicitly `public static final` constants and interfaces cannot have constructors, whereas an abstract class can hold mutable instance state and constructors.

questions.question: Which query correctly lists all customers from `Customers c` who have placed ZERO orders in `Orders o` (even if `Orders.cust_id` contains `NULL`s)?
options: `SELECT c.id FROM Customers c WHERE c.id NOT IN (SELECT cust_id FROM Orders)`
`SELECT c.id FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.cust_id WHERE o.cust_id IS NULL`
`SELECT c.id FROM Customers c INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.id <> o.cust_id`
`SELECT c.id FROM Customers c RIGHT JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.cust_id WHERE c.id IS NULL`
questions.explanation: `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE o.cust_id IS NULL` (or `NOT EXISTS`) safely finds unmatched rows regardless of `NULL`s in `Orders.cust_id`, whereas `NOT IN` returns 0 rows if any `cust_id` is `NULL`.

questions.subtopic: Doubly Linked List vs Singly Linked List
questions.question: Given ONLY a direct pointer `node` to an arbitrary middle node inside a list (and no head pointer), in which structure can `node` be deleted in `O(1)` time without copying data from the next node?
options: Doubly Linked List (using `node.prev.next = node.next` and `node.next.prev = node.prev`)
questions.explanation: A doubly linked list maintains `prev` pointers, enabling `O(1)` unlinking of any given node directly without scanning from `head`.

questions.question: Which data structure does the OS kernel update to save a preempted process's Program Counter, CPU registers, and memory-management state?
questions.explanation: Each process's execution context (registers, PC, scheduling priority, open files, page table pointer) is stored in its Process Control Block (PCB).

questions.question: Why does HTTPS use asymmetric cryptography (RSA/ECDHE) during the TLS handshake, and then switch to symmetric encryption (AES-GCM / ChaCha20) for bulk HTTP data?
options: Symmetric keys cannot be used on TCP port 443
Asymmetric crypto authenticates the server and safely establishes a shared session key, while symmetric crypto encrypts bulk traffic orders of magnitude faster
Symmetric encryption requires zero CPU cycles
Browsers cannot store symmetric keys in RAM
questions.explanation: Asymmetric key exchange solves identity verification and key agreement over an untrusted network; symmetric authenticated encryption handles high-throughput payload encryption efficiently.

questions.question: Predict the exact console output produced by signed (`>>`) versus unsigned (`>>>`) right bit-shifting on a negative integer in Java:
questions.explanation: `>>` is signed arithmetic right shift (preserves sign bit `1`, so `-8 >> 1 == -4`). `>>>` is unsigned logical right shift (fills MSB with `0`, turning negative `0xFFFFFFF8` into positive `0x7FFFFFFC = 2147483644`).
